thesis: Jayson Tatum struggled with shooting efficiency after returning from torn Achilles surgery mid-season 2025-26, adjusting to a reduced offensive role as secondary option behind Jaylen Brown while the Celtics contended for the East title.

facts.claim: Tatum suffered a torn Achilles in the 2025 NBA playoffs and accelerated his return to take a secondary role behind Jaylen Brown.
After returning, Tatum described his shooting slump as unprecedented, stating he had never experienced something like it before.
Tatum appeared uncomfortable on court readjusting to an offense where he functions as a role-player while testing his newly-healed Achilles.
In 2026 playoffs, Tatum shot 40.6% from the floor, ranking fifth among Boston's rotation players, and 25% from three-point range.
Coach Brad Stevens and analysts suggested moving Tatum away from isolation and pick-and-roll handling to more off-ball forward role.
The Celtics maintained a 126.4 offensive rating with Tatum on court in 2026 playoffs versus 101.7 when he sat, despite his reduced scoring.
